Naomi / team —

Below is a suggested set of edits I think will be acceptable to procurement while protecting HelioTech's asks. These are drafted for insertion into the Order Form (or MSA publicity appendix), marked with bracketed text to be finalized:

1) Embargo: 'The parties agree not to publicly announce or disclose the existence of this Agreement or the business relationship contemplated hereby for a period of fourteen (14) calendar days following the date of the final, mutually agreed written announcement (the "Embargo Period"), unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing.'

2) Logo use: 'Redwood may use Customer's name and logo solely for Redwood's marketing collateral, website, and press materials, subject to Customer's prior written approval for each use (approval not to be unreasonably withheld). Customer shall not be required to approve use in paid advertising, solicitations, or sponsored content without separate written consent.'

3) Testimonials and quotes: 'Redwood shall not publish direct quotes attributed to Customer or use Customer's logo in promotional materials containing Customer quotations without Customer's prior written consent. Use of Customer's name as a factual reference in a customer list or case study is permitted with prior notice.'

4) Approval route: 'All approvals shall be routed to legal@heliotech.com and may be actioned by either an authorized in-house counsel or a named company representative for operational approvals (e.g., Samira Khan).'

I also recommend adding a simple approval SLA: 'Customer will respond to approval requests within seven (7) business days. Failure to respond shall be deemed approval for non-sensitive marketing uses.' That helps prevent open loops.

Flagging one risk: the 'approval not to be unreasonably withheld' language can be contentious for some security-minded customers. If HelioTech insists on 'approval in writing' with no qualifier, Redwood should ask for a narrower carveout for press announcements tied to joint case studies.

If you want, I can produce a tracked-redline of HT-OrderForm_v3 with these clauses inserted.

—Rishi
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — that reads well overall. A couple of comments from Legal:
- They prefer 'approval not to be unreasonably withheld' removed and instead request a 'defined approval process' with the 7 business day SLA you suggested.
- For logo use in case studies, HelioTech wants the ability to review and request redactions for any technical diagrams pulled from their environment.

We can accept the 14-day embargo. Regarding paid ads, we agree to a separate discussion but prefer a default 'no use in paid advertising' unless expressly permitted.

Samira

On a practical note: can Redwood attach an example 'publicity blurb' that you would use? HelioTech wants to see phrasing before we give pre-approval.
